proposals.before: Once he received the edict, he became ever more utterly loyal and careful, spoke freely of whatever he knew, and his perquisites grew ever more numerous.
proposals.after: Once he received the edict, he became ever more utterly loyal and careful, spoke freely of whatever he knew, and his beneficial counsel was abundant.
proposals.reason: 便益為多 refers to abundant beneficial advice/measures, not personal perquisites.

decisions.reason: Chinese 〈（藥師奴）〉 is a parenthetical name gloss; the English retains stray ]〉 from the annotation brackets and must be cleaned to (Yaoshinu).
Same corruption as the idiomatic field: literal English keeps leftover ]〉 after (Yaoshinu) while the Chinese is only the nested gloss 〈（藥師奴）〉.
After 知無不言, 便益為多 means the beneficial counsel or measures he offered were many, not that his personal perquisites increased; the proposed replacement restores that sense.
